method.name: Welch's one-way ANOVA
method.evaluates: Whether the mean of the measurement differs across three or more groups, without assuming the groups have equal variances.
method.null_hypothesis: All groups have equal population means.
assumptions: Each row is treated as an independent observation. Paired or repeated measurements of the same subject are not supported.

Each group's mean is approximately normally distributed: the values are roughly normal, or the group is large enough for the central limit theorem to apply. Strong skew or outliers in small groups make the p-value unreliable.
Group variances may differ. This is Welch's (1951) ANOVA, not the classical F-test, which assumes equal variances.
Each group needs at least two values with some variation, because groups are weighted by their size divided by their variance.
limitations: The overall test says whether at least one group mean differs; it does not identify which groups differ. Pairwise (post-hoc) comparisons are not provided.
A p-value above the chosen significance level does not show the groups are equal; it means this data did not provide clear evidence of a difference.
Eta squared describes the share of variation between group means in this sample; it does not adjust for unequal variances.

test.reason: Welch's ANOVA is offered for three or more groups; this selection has two. Request welch_t_test, which runs the equivalent test and also returns the mean difference and its confidence interval.

response.note: Each row is treated as an independent observation. Paired or repeated measurements of the same subject are not supported.

analysis_question.text: Does the mean of 'score' differ across the 'group' groups?

box_plot.whisker_rule: Tukey: whiskers reach the most extreme values within 1.5 x IQR of the quartiles.
box_plot.outliers: Values beyond the whiskers are counted in outlier_count.
